title: DC-area forecast: Some sun is back today as temperatures slowly warm into Friday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: A crisp, breezy start comes with a welcome return of at least partial sunshine after days of gloom. Highs reach the low to mid-60s.

What’s next? Around 70 tomorrow after a seasonably cool night tonight. Some questions remain about an offshore storm this weekend, but we should stay on the edge of it at worst.

Today’s daily digit — 6/10: Partial sunshine feels like a big win after several days dominated by rain and clouds. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Thursday): Sun makes a comeback, at least partially. It's still on the cool side, with highs reaching the low to mid-60s. Winds blow out of the northeast around 10 mph, with gusts near 20 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: Partly cloudy skies have enough clearing for lows to fall farther than recent nights, reaching the upper 40s to low 50s. Winds are from the north around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): Looking pretty nice, if also on the breezy side. A coastal low well offshore helps crank up our winds from the north to around 15 mph, with gusts near 25 to 30 mph. But skies should be mainly sunny, with highs ending up within a few degrees of 70. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow night: Partly to mostly clear and still breezy. Temperatures fall to lows in the 50s. Confidence: Medium-High

❤️ How to support Capital Weather

Help sustain an independent Capital Weather by becoming a free or paid supporter. Learn more at capitalweather.com/support-us

A look ahead

Still some question marks for the weekend with a strong storm system centered offshore. It should stay far enough away that we remain mostly or entirely dry, though some rain could reach into especially eastern and northeastern parts of the region later Saturday into Sunday. Sunnier scenarios allow highs to reach 70 to 75, while more clouds and a shower chance could hold highs in the mid-60s to near 70. Saturday seems like the warmer of the two. Winds from the north gust around 25 mph. Confidence: Medium

The meandering coastal low should be moving away more decisively by Monday, meaning diminishing breezes and increasing sunshine. Warmer temperatures also become more likely, with highs around the mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

College Park tornado
